facts.statement: The specific name espinosai honors the Mexican paleontologist and researcher Luis Espinosa.
facts.quote: The specific name, espinosai, honors Mexican paleontologist and researcher Luis Espinosa.

facts.statement: Xenovenator lived during the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) age.
Xenovenator possessed a thickened dome on its cranium formed by the frontal bones.
facts.quote: The preserved cranial bones of Xenovenator indicate that the cranium bore a thickened dome formed by the frontal bones.

facts.statement: Rivera-Sylva et al. interpreted the dome expansion and fusion as possible evidence of ontogenetic variation, occurring as the animal matured.
facts.quote: Rivera-Sylva et al. (2026) interpreted this as possible evidence of ontogenetic variation, with the dome expanding and fusing as the animal matured.

facts.statement: An alternative explanation for the dome is sexual dimorphism, an occurrence common in extant mammals and birds but not well-documented in non-avian dinosaurs.
facts.quote: An alternative proposed explanation is sexual dimorphism, an occurrence not well-documented in non-avian dinosaurs but common in extant mammals and birds.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis recovered Xenovenator in a late-diverging position within the clade Troodontinae.
facts.quote: Xenovenator was recovered in a late-diverging position within the more exclusive clade Troodontinae.

facts.statement: Jasinski & Sullivan later placed X.? robustus in the new genus Dinevenator in the same year.
facts.quote: Later that year, Jasinski & Sullivan placed X.? robustus in a new genus, Dinevenator.

facts.statement: Martha C. Aguillón-Martínez collected a partial theropod skull during fieldwork in the Cerro del Pueblo Formation at La Parrita, Coahuila, Mexico, in the summer of 2000.
facts.quote: Durante el trabajo de campo en la Formación Cerro del Pueblo (localidad de La Parrita) en Coahuila, México, en el verano de 2000, Martha C. Aguillón-Martínez recolectó el cráneo parcial de un dinosaurio terópodo.

facts.statement: Martha C. Aguillón-Martínez and Héctor E. Rivera-Sylva described specimen CPC 2973 in 2023.
facts.quote: En 2023, Aguillón-Martínez describió CPC 2973 en colaboración con Héctor E. Rivera-Sylva.

facts.statement: Xenovenator belongs to the parent group Troodontini.
Xenovenator is classified in the family Troodontidae.
Xenovenator is classified in the class Reptilia.
Xenovenator lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Xenovenator is characterized by a thickened and domed skull roof found in the Campanian Cerro del Pueblo Formation of Coahuila, Mexico.
The domed cranium and extremely thick bones of Xenovenator represent a morphology convergent with Pachycephalosauridae.
Variation in skull thickening and doming among referred specimens suggests either ontogenetic changes or sexual dimorphism.
Researchers hypothesize that the skull specializations of Xenovenator indicate adaptation for intraspecific combat, specifically head-butting.
Initially, the partial skull was considered an indeterminate member of the troodontid family and was not named until later.
facts.quote: Los autores explicaron que el cráneo parcial representa el primer material fósil no dental de un troodóntido descrito en México, pero lo consideraron como un miembro indeterminado de la familia, sin nombrarlo.
